novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new-channel hypothesis—“the student's policy acquires the reward model's hidden trait” from “a single trait-free number” with “zero teacher tokens in the loss”—plus the mechanistic predictions that the matched-base gate moves to reward-model↔policy and that RL follows the same early-layer trait direction as SFT. Searches around “subliminal learning scalar reward reinforcement learning,” “RLHF reward poisoning hidden trait transfer,” and “matched-base reward model policy” identify Cloud et al., “Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data,” as the closest phenomenon work and RLHFPoison (2023) and “Backdoors in RLVR” (2026) as the closest reward-channel security work; the former is confined to distillation on teacher outputs, while the latter directly poison rewards or training examples rather than transmitting a latent disposition through semantically unrelated scoring. Moving subliminal learning from token imitation to scalar optimization is therefore a non-trivial natural extension and integration, while the relocated gate and shared-direction predictions add new relationships, but these are largely adaptations of Cloud et al.'s matched-base and early-layer findings rather than a wholly new mechanistic paradigm.
